rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
The cell membrane regulates what enters and exits the cell via passive and active transport.
Mitochondria generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation in the electron transport chain.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The cell membrane is fluid mosaic model – a dynamic arrangement of lipids and proteins.  ·  Mitochondrial DNA is circular and similar to bacterial DNA, supporting endosymbiotic theory.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Chloroplasts contain thylakoids where light-dependent reactions occur.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Nucleus: controls cell activities, contains DNA  ·  Mitochondria: powerhouse of the cell (ATP production)

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Cell Theory Recap  ·  - All living organisms are composed of one or more cells

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Cell membrane is selectively permeable – small molecules diffuse freely, large molecules need carriers.  ·  Mitochondria = powerhouse of the cell (produces ATP).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: What is the function of the rough endoplasmic reticulum?  ·  Why do mitochondria have their own DNA?

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Cell theory has three postulates: 1) All living things are made of cells, 2) Cells are the basic unit of structure/function, 3) New cells come from existing cells.  ·  Organelle function questions commonly appear – match organelle to its primary function.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Ribosomes: protein synthesis machinery (70S in prokaryotes, 80S in eukaryotes)  ·  Endoplasmic reticulum: RER (protein synthesis), SER (lipid synthesis)  ·  Golgi apparatus: modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins/lipids  ·  Lysosomes: digestive compartments containing hydrolytic enzymes

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Organelles have specific functions: nucleus (control), mitochondria (energy), ER (synthesis), Golgi (packaging), lysosomes (digestion).  ·  Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles but have a nucleoid region with DNA.  ·  Eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus surrounded by a nuclear envelope.

rows.text: What is the difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Compare prokaryotic vs eukaryotic cell structures in exam questions.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: - The cell is the basic unit of structure and function  ·  - All cells arise from pre-existing cells (Virchow: omnis cellula e cellula)  ·  - Cells can be prokaryotic (no nucleus) or eukaryotic (nucleus present)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Chloroplasts: site of photosynthesis (plant cells only)  ·  Centrosome: organizes microtubules in animal cells  ·  Eukaryotic cells are larger (10-100 µm) than prokaryotic cells (1-10 µm).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis, translating mRNA into polypeptide chains.  ·  Ribosomes are found on rough ER and free in cytoplasm.  ·  Chloroplasts are only in plant cells and algae.
